title: The Dog and the Shadow
originalTitle: Greek title not preserved in this edition
place: A plank over a running brook
sourceAuthor: Aesop; selected and told anew by Joseph Jacobs

artLabel: A dog carrying meat crosses a plank above his reflection.
scenes: It happened that a Dog had got a piece of meat and was carrying it home in his mouth to eat it in peace.

Now on his way home he had to cross a plank lying across a running brook. As he crossed, he looked down and saw his own shadow reflected in the water beneath. Thinking it was another dog with another piece of meat, he made up his mind to have that also.
So he made a snap at the shadow in the water, but as he opened his mouth the piece of meat fell out, dropped into the water and was never seen more.
Beware lest you lose the substance by grasping at the shadow.

pageArt.alt: The dog looks down from the plank and sees another piece of meat in the water.
The dog watches the lost meat sink into the running brook.
